text:
**My pick is the Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand.** WIRED named it best overall after testing 30+ models. I couldn't open store pages here, so most links below go to the review pages, which have the current buy buttons.

**Top picks**

| Need | Pick | Price (per the sources) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand | $109 list, about $80-98 at retailers | 15W iPhone charging, tilting pad, landscape/StandBy support, 2-year warranty, and a 36W adapter included |
| Fastest | Nomad Stand One Max | $169 | 25W Qi2 for iPhone, but no power adapter is included, so you need a 40W one (about $25 extra) |
| Budget | ESR Qi2 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station | about $40 on sale ($80 list) | 15W, adapter and cable included, 1-year warranty. The Watch charger is a separate slot-in piece, and the reviewer lost its cap |
| Flat, out-of-sight charging | Nimble Podium 3-in-1 | $130 | Qi2 25W, but Apple Watch charging is slow, so it's best overnight |

Sources: [WIRED's best 3-in-1 chargers](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)

**If you travel**

- **Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (Qi2):** WIRED's best travel pick, about $80 on sale, folds slim, 15W. [WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/)
- **Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable (Qi2 25W):** $129.99, with a 45W adapter and UK/EU plugs included. Macworld says it's the tallest and most adjustable foldable, which makes it good as a desk stand too, but it weighs about 399g. [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html)
- **ESR CryoBoost 25W:** about $100, with a quiet fan you can switch off. WIRED found the plastic build less premium. [Buy via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand). Dealectric lists it at $99.99, or $82 with code PARTNER18 (tested 2026-10-23, expires 2026-12-31). Dealectric earns a commission, and it says this is the only product in its own records, not the best overall.

**Which speed do you need?**
- 25W only helps with newer iPhones. Per Dealectric's ESR listing, the iPhone 17 series, 16 Pro Max and 16 Plus get 25W (iOS 26 required), the iPhone Air, 16 and 16 Pro get 20W, and older models get 15W.
- WIRED and Macworld both say 25W makes little difference if you charge overnight, so the Belkin or the budget ESR is plenty for most people.
- Check that your AirPods case supports wireless charging, since the base pad only works with those.

If you tell me your iPhone model and whether this is for a nightstand, desk or travel, I can narrow it to one.
